title: One-Eye Two-Eyes Three-Eyes final

full_text:
A mother had three daughters: One-Eye had a single eye in her forehead; Three-Eyes had three eyes; and Two-Eyes looked like an ordinary human maiden. Because Two-Eyes was normal and beautiful, her grotesque sisters despised her, dressing her in rags and giving her only leftovers.

Weeping in the meadow, Two-Eyes was comforted by a wise woodland fairy, who taught her a magic rhyme to speak to her little goat: "Little goat, bleat, little table, appear!" Instantly, a spotless table covered with delicate roasted meats and sweet pastries appeared. When finished, she said: "Little goat, bleat, little table, depart!" and it vanished.

Suspicious of how Two-Eyes looked so healthy, the sisters sent One-Eye to spy. Two-Eyes sang One-Eye to sleep, but when Three-Eyes went, Two-Eyes forgot to sing to the third eye! Three-Eyes saw the magic and told their mother, who killed the gentle goat.

The fairy instructed Two-Eyes to bury the goat's heart beneath the garden gate. The next morning, a magnificent tree with leaves of pure silver and apples of pure gold had grown there! Neither One-Eye nor Three-Eyes could pluck a single fruit—the branches sprang out of their grasp. But when Two-Eyes reached up, the golden apples dropped gently into her apron.

A handsome knight rode by and asked for the golden fruit. Two-Eyes presented the apples to the noble knight. Enchanted by her grace and gentle spirit, the knight married Two-Eyes and took her to his castle, where she lived in joy, forgiving her cruel sisters when they came begging in poverty.
moral: The gentle and pure heart is exalted above cruel vanity and jealous torment.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "One-Eye Two-Eyes Three-Eyes final"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
